transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

To be honest, I’m only really here because my family pressured me to get evaluated. I just can’t shake this constant fear of putting on weight, so I keep cutting back on what I eat, even though my wife and kids say I’m already too thin.

Do you believe you are overweight or have a strong fear of gaining weight even when others say you are underweight? Or do you mainly just have little interest in food without much concern about your body shape?

It’s definitely a strong fear of gaining weight, not just a lack of interest in food. Even though my wife says I'm too thin and is overreacting, I get this rush of panic that I'll balloon up overnight if I eat a normal meal. That fear makes me constantly check the scale and cut back on eating just to keep control.
Have you had any episodes of binge eating or vomiting, using laxatives, or other behaviors to prevent weight gain?

No, I’ve never done anything like that—no binge eating, throwing up, or using laxatives. My only focus is strictly on cutting back on what I eat and keeping a close eye on the scale. I just want to keep the weight down by eating less.

Do you feel that your body weight or shape is too large even when other people tell you that you are underweight, or do you recognize that you are very thin but still feel unable to eat more because of the fear of gaining weight?

I don't really see myself as too large, and I actually feel pretty proud when people say I look lean or "shredded." I think my family is overreacting about me being too thin, but I just can't bring myself to eat more because of the intense panic I feel about gaining weight. Even a tiny increase on the scale makes me feel like I'll balloon up overnight.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview is most consistent with anorexia nervosa: there is a persistent and intense fear of gaining weight, restrictive intake to prevent weight gain, marked concern with weight/shape, and acknowledgment of being very thin by others. The patient denies binge eating, purging, or laxative use, supporting the restrictive type. No evidence was provided for an alternative eating disorder diagnosis.
